key_insight: ColdDDI shows that cold-start DDI models perform much better when a shared enzyme, transporter, or target is available, revealing that mechanistic evidence—not just model size—drives success.
clinical_relevance: This matters for safer medication review because models should be judged on whether they can use pharmacologic evidence to flag interactions for drugs with little or no prior interaction history.
method: Built ColdDDI from DrugBank 5.1.13 with 1,900 approved drugs and 565,731 positive DDI pairs.
Evaluated zero-, one-, and two-unseen-drug splits to test cold-start prediction.
Probed 8 DDI methods and 13 LLMs using masking, drug replacement, and channel-sensitivity tests to measure knowledge use.
evidence_signal: In the hardest split with two unseen drugs, fine-tuned 1B LLMs recovered 89-93% of interactions with a shared mediator but only 40-62% without one.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific and do not guarantee safe real-world clinical use, especially for interactions not represented by the knowledge graph.
paper_title: ColdDDI: Evaluating Knowledge Utilization in Cold-Start Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction
